why: The board cites Jenkins's greater experience running county operations and crisis response; it calls Immler a serious candidate with good ideas on procurement.
The board credits Meyer's work on property tax cuts as Ways and Means chair and his flood-safety work; it calls Mitchell capable but not his match.
The board cites Button's experience and independence from her party; it calls Herbert well prepared but less developed on education.
The board says Hernandez has learned the House quickly and written useful bills on housing, insurance and health; her opponent skipped its interview.
The board prefers Clark's focus on literacy and her experience, while saying it disagrees with her on vouchers; it worries Garza would add religious instruction.
The board cites Taylor's classroom experience and practical views; it says Bumgarner did not respond to its questionnaire or interview.
The board says Reichek, who served on this court from 2019 to 2024, would restore needed experience; it calls Kolodoski qualified but outmatched.
The board calls both judges strong and "tips toward" Smith for his judicial philosophy and broader general-jurisdiction experience.
The board, which says it usually opposes tax increases, backs Housing Forward's plan to scale its downtown results countywide and promises to hold it accountable.
The board explicitly declined to recommend either Amber Givens or write-in Eric Reed, citing concerns about both.
The board explicitly offered no recommendation, saying neither Huddleston nor Ledferd is the serious, outcome-focused member the board wants.
